title: Symbol & photography
slide_intent: Teach designers to decide whether a symbol should reveal a picture or join the scene. Each technique gives the viewer a different way to find the person in the photograph.
strategic_value: Frontline AIDS can connect the same figure to lived experience through a recognizable silhouette or a graphic presence in a portrait.
demonstration: On a cyan page, a tall photograph is visible through the outlined person shape, while a second portrait sits beside an oversized green figure. An outdoor panel shows a wider application.
practical_value: Use a figure-shaped frame when the crop still communicates its subject; use integration when a figure can sit beside the photographed person.

content_islands.name: Two techniques
content_islands.spec: Introduce the two photography approaches in the left text field, then place the framed portrait centrally and the integrated example across the lower right.

content_islands.spec: Place the smaller billboard photograph under the introduction so the cropped figure can be compared at street scale.
